Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals · Section 15.7 · Exercise 18

A Triple Integral over a Cylindrical Wedge in the First Octant

Problem

Evaluate the triple integral

∭E​zdV,

where E is bounded by the cylinder y2+z2=9 and the planes x=0, y=3x, and z=0 in the first octant.

Reading the solid

The equation y2+z2=9 describes a circular cylinder of radius 3 whose axis is the x-axis. A point of this cylinder has distance 3 from the x-axis, whatever its x-coordinate is. The plane z=0 and the first octant keep only the part above the xy-plane, so every cross-section of E parallel to the yz-plane is a quarter of the disk y2+z2≤9.

The plane x=0 is the back wall. The plane y=3x is a vertical plane through the z-axis; it cuts the xy-plane along the line y=3x. The condition x≥0, together with the cylinder, limits y to the interval 0≤y≤3, because the cylinder meets the xy-plane at y=3. The plane y=3x then gives x≤y/3, and at the far rim y=3 this bound is x=1.

Therefore E projects onto the triangle

Dxy​={(x,y):0≤y≤3,0≤x≤y/3},

with vertices (0,0), (1,3), and (0,3). Above a point (x,y) of this triangle the solid reaches from the floor z=0 up to the cylinder wall z=9−y2​. The top does not depend on x, because the cylinder is parallel to the x-axis.

Two projections make the limits visible. The left panel below shows Dxy​, the triangle in which y runs from 0 to 3 and x runs from 0 to y/3. The right panel shows the quarter disk in the yz-plane that gives the height z=9−y2​ of each slice.

These two pictures give one description of E:

E={(x,y,z):0≤y≤3,0≤x≤y/3,0≤z≤9−y2​}.

Solution

Step 1 — Set up the iterated integral

The description fixes the order dzdxdy. The inner variable is z, the middle variable is x, and the outer variable is y:

∭E​zdV=∫03​∫0y/3​∫09−y2​​zdzdxdy.

Step 2 — Integrate with respect to z

The inner integral has the antiderivative z2/2, so

∫09−y2​​zdz=[2z2​]09−y2​​=29−y2​.

Step 3 — Integrate with respect to x

The result of Step 2 depends only on y. The inner limit of the x-range is 0 and the outer limit is y/3, so the x-integration multiplies by the width y/3:

∫0y/3​29−y2​dx=29−y2​⋅3y​=6y(9−y2)​=69y−y3​.

The factor 1/6 is the product of the factor 1/2 from the z-integral and the factor 1/3 from the width y/3.

Step 4 — Integrate with respect to y

The outer integral is a polynomial integral:

∫03​69y−y3​dy=61​[29y2​−4y4​]03​.

At y=3 the bracket is

29⋅9​−481​=4162​−481​=481​,

and at y=0 the bracket is zero. Hence

∭E​zdV=61​⋅481​=2481​=827​.

Step 5 — Check the result with a second order

Reverse the two outer integrations. A point of Dxy​ has 0≤x≤1, and for a fixed x the other coordinate runs from the line y=3x to the rim y=3:

∫01​∫3x3​∫09−y2​​zdzdydx=∫01​∫3x3​29−y2​dydx=∫01​21​[9y−3y3​]3x3​dx=827​.

Both orders give 27/8, so the limits of Step 1 are correct. A third check uses the sections perpendicular to the y-axis. The section at a fixed y is a rectangle of area

A(y)=3y​9−y2​,

and ∫03​A(y)dy=3 is the volume of E. The integral of z is the same sum weighted by the mean height z of each section, and that weighted sum returns 27/8.

Answer

∭E​zdV=827​=3.375.

Notation

SymbolMeaning
∭E​fdVThe triple integral of the function f over the solid region E; it is the limit of sums of f times small volumes.
EThe solid of integration: the set of points in the first octant that satisfy the three given inequalities.
dVThe volume element. In Cartesian coordinates dV=dzdxdy, the product of the three coordinate differentials in the chosen order.
y2+z2=9A circular cylinder of radius 3 about the x-axis: every point of it is at distance 3 from that axis.
first octantThe part of space where x≥0, y≥0, and z≥0.
Dxy​The projection of E onto the xy-plane, here the triangle 0≤y≤3, 0≤x≤y/3.
9−y2​The height of the cylinder wall above the point (x,y) of the floor; it does not depend on x.
A(y)The area of the section of E at a fixed value of y, a rectangle of width y/3 and height 9−y2​.
ΔyThe thickness of one slice in the figure; the slices approximate E, and the sum of their volumes becomes the integral as Δy→0.

Verification

Three independent computations support the result.

  • part1_step1.py checks the three bounding surfaces and estimates the integral by Monte Carlo sampling in the box 0≤x≤1, 0≤y≤3, 0≤z≤3. The estimate is 3.36825 against the exact value 3.37500, a deviation of −2.22 standard errors with standard error 0.00305. The sampled fraction inside E is 0.33279, close to the ratio 3/9 of the volume of E to the volume of the box.
  • part1_step2.py repeats the evaluation with SymPy. It returns the inner integral 9/2−y2/2, the middle integral y(9−y2)/6, the bracket value 81/4 at y=3, and the total 27/8=3.375000000000. The section check returns the area y9−y2​/3 and the volume 3.
  • part1_step3.py evaluates the integral with mpmath quadrature at 25 digits in two orders, dzdxdy and dzdydx. Both values are 3.375, with a deviation of 0.0 from 27/8.
